issues.legal_issue: Compensation for acquired land must be assessed by reference to comparable acquisitions from the relevant period, rather than a higher award arising from a materially later acquisition or an unnoticed mistake.
material_facts: The land was acquired in 1976, and the landowners challenged the compensation determined by the Land Acquisition Officer and the Reference Court.

The landowners sought compensation at the rate awarded in Mangu, which principally concerned land acquired in 1991; certain appeals concerning 1977 acquisitions had been disposed of with that case without the acquisition-year difference being noticed.

The High Court’s award in Jagmal of a higher rate for a 1976 acquisition was later reviewed and reduced to the rate consistently awarded for 1976–1977 acquisitions; that reviewed determination was confirmed by the Supreme Court.
Several other decisions concerning acquisitions in 1976–1977, including acquisitions in the same or nearby villages, fixed compensation at the same rate.
The landowners alternatively relied on an award for land acquired in 1983, but development had taken place after 1980 and a development plan was in place by the time of that acquisition.
issues.conclusion: The appeals were partly allowed, and compensation for the land acquired in 1976 was enhanced to Rs.28.12 per square yard, with applicable statutory benefits on the enhanced compensation. The higher awards relied on by the landowners did not justify compensation at Rs.297 per square yard.
issues.legal_principle: In determining compensation on a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, the relevant basis is comparable land and circumstances at the time of the acquisition; compensation awarded for a materially later acquisition is not comparable merely because a depreciation formula is proposed, particularly where development occurred in the intervening period. A party cannot claim parity from an award that resulted from an inadvertent failure to notice material differences in the acquisitions. The Court relied on the reviewed determination in Jagmal and the consistent determinations for 1976–1977 acquisitions, while distinguishing Mangu and Khazan because of the different acquisition periods and circumstances.

predicates.land_acquisition_compensation_appeal: The landowners appealed a determination of compensation for land acquired by the government.
predicates.claimed_comparator_is_from_materially_la: The landowners relied on an award for land acquired materially later than their land, after intervening development or other relevant changes.
predicates.claimed_comparator_award_reflects_unnoti: The landowners relied on an award that was made without the court noticing a material difference in the acquisition periods or circumstances.
predicates.comparable_same_period_awards_support_an: Other decisions concerning comparable acquisitions from the relevant period consistently supported a different compensation rate.

issues.definition: When landowners appeal a compensation determination, a materially later award or one made without noticing a material acquisition difference does not displace the rate supported by comparable awards from the relevant period.
